title: Release quiet-windows and telemetry sampling plan (Jul 2026) - WIP
content:
Context and goal:

This working doc captures a proposed operational playbook for scheduling release quiet-windows across regions and implementing telemetry sampling during high-risk rollouts. Goal: reduce noise to on-call, ensure representative telemetry for canaries and early-stage rollouts, and provide a repeatable scheduler for cross-team coordination (release-eng, SRE, product-hosted-api, infra).

Why this is different: previous rollout documents focus on cutover steps and fallbacks. This one fixes two gaps we keep hitting in Q2–Q3 2026:
- noisy false-positive alerts during large batch deployments (prefix cache flushes, model warmups)
- telemetry overload that skews early metric signals when sampling is inconsistent between regions/tiers

High-level approach (summary):
1) Define 'quiet-window' behavior per service (alerts throttled, non-actionable alerts suppressed, longer symptom aggregation windows)
2) Apply telemetry sampling rules during quiet-windows for non-critical traces/metrics
3) Provide an explicit, visible calendar with region + timezone windows and owner tags to avoid overlapping changes across dependent systems
4) Rollout the policy progressively (lab -> staging -> small production segment -> global) with checks at each step

Operational definitions:
- Quiet-window: a scheduled time window around a release when non-actionable low-severity alerts are suppressed and runbooks are put on hold for non-blocking ops. Severity thresholds are temporarily raised for alerts that historically flood during deployments. Critical (P0/P1) alerts still page immediately.
- Telemetry sampling: for high-cardinality, high-volume signals (detailed traces, debug-level logs, per-token latency histograms), reduce sampling to a consistent percentage and annotate events with rollout_id and sample_bucket to allow downstream inflation correction.

Suggested quiet-window templates (choose based on expected impact):
- Small patch (non-model binary change): 30m pre, 45m post, 0.5x sampling for debug traces
- Medium release (config + minor infra change): 1h pre, 2h post, 0.25x sampling for traces, 0.5x for logs
- Model swap / major infra: 2h pre, 6h post, 0.1x sampling for traces, 0.25x for logs, enable telemetry parity checks

Telemetry sampling rules (implementation notes):
- Default sampling implementation should be in the telemetry ingest layer (observability pipeline) not in the application code. Tag sampled events with rollout_id and sample_rate.
- Sampling bucketing: deterministic hash(event_id || rollout_id) mod 100 to ensure repeatable buckets across retries and regions.
- Ensure metrics that are aggregated (error rate, latencies) include sample_rate multiplier in downstream aggregator so dashboards show corrected values.
- For embeddings/sequence-level signals, sample at the request-level not token-level to preserve correlation.

Quiet-window ops checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] Announce window in #release-coord and update the shared calendar (owner + timezone)
- [ ] Confirm cross-team dependencies (S3 migration, database migrations). Tag teams in calendar event
- [ ] Configure observability: set sampling flag for target services, open a short-lived telemetry dashboard annotated for rollout_id
- [ ] Prepare rollback artifacts: rollback instructions, warm backups, canary endpoints, and hotfix PR template
- [ ] Run quick smoke tests in staging with sampling enabled to validate metric correction pipeline

During release (live checklist):
- [ ] 30m before: put non-blocking runbooks to 'snooze' (notify on-call)
- [ ] 10m before: set sampling flags in ingest (feature flag toggle), toggle alert thresholds per template
- [ ] Launch canary segment (targeted customers/region) and monitor annotated dashboard
- [ ] After canary success: incrementally expand to next percentage bucket (per rollout schedule)
- [ ] If any P1/P0 triggers: abort expansion, execute rollback plan, and keep debug sampling at 1x to capture full fidelity

Post-deploy (post-window checklist):
- [ ] Keep sampling at reduced rate for the post window period, then restore to baseline at the end of the post window
- [ ] Annotate the release notes (see section below) with sampling and quiet-window parameters used
- [ ] Run aggregated telemetry parity check: compare pre-release baselines vs. sampled-corrected metrics. If drift > threshold, create postmortem ticket

Rollout calendar and ownership (example template for a single week):
- Mon 2026-07-12 02:00 UTC — Hosted API minor release — Owner: Ava S. — Quiet-window: 00:30/00:45 — Sampling: traces 50%
- Tue 2026-07-13 08:00 UTC — Dedicated infra patch — Owner: Jordan M. — Quiet-window: 01:00/02:00 — Sampling: traces 25%
- Thu 2026-07-15 22:00 UTC — Private deploy (customer X) — Owner: Samira K. — Quiet-window: 02:00/04:00 — Sampling: traces 10%

Rollout notes (draft language for release changelog):
- Brief: "Routing + batching kernel update to improve cold-start latency. Deployed under quiet-window and telemetry sampling; sampling rate set to 25% for debug traces."
- Observability: link to rollout dashboard and annotated alerts.
- Backout criteria: "If request-level p95 latency increases > 20% for 10 minutes or error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, initiate rollback workflow (see RELEASE-874)."

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sampling mismatch between regions leads to biased metrics. Mitigation: deterministic bucketing by rollout_id, and parity checks within 30m of each expansion step.
- Risk: Suppressing alerts masks real incidents. Mitigation: only low-severity alerts suppressed; critical alerts unchanged. Pre-flight verification of alert mappings required.
- Risk: Telemetry pipeline downstream tools mis-handle sample_rate tags. Mitigation: QA in staging and a small canary with full-fidelity telemetry before wide expansion.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the centralized calendar maintenance? Proposal: release-eng duty rotates weekly but bookings require SRE co-approval.
- Can we add a lightweight UI in Redwood Console to annotate rollouts with rollout_id (product request)? Ticket: R-1234
- Determine final list of alerts considered "non-actionable" during quiet-windows — need input from product-hosted-api and observability teams

Action items (owners):
- Riley: finalize sampling flag implementation doc and add feature-flag toggles to runtime repo (due 2026-07-16)
- Jordan: prepare staging QA plan for sample-corrected dashboards (due 2026-07-14)
- Samira: coordinate with customer success for any private deploys overlapping this week (due 2026-07-10)

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Might be worth a small script that automatically annotates new dashboard queries with sample_rate multipliers for quick eyeballing.
- Consider a default global policy for low-traffic regions to avoid repeated calendar friction.

References and links:
- Observability sampling best-practices (internal Confluence) — link placeholder
- Runtime PR that added sampling flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412
- Related Linear ticket: R-1234

Status: draft/WIP. This doc should be converted into a release checklist template and a calendar event template once agreed.

End of doc.
